0.reason: the document's own second experiment and its reproduction state that the rollback acts only against a pre-landing HEAD; the sentence describes the reverted state persisting while HEAD carried the landing, and a reader of the document is not left with the other reading

findings.text: follow-on: the timeline states 'the reversal happened while HEAD already carried the landing', but the document's own second experiment (and scripts/reproduce_landing_reversion.py) establishes that _restore_landing_writes changes nothing when HEAD already carries the landing and only acts on a pre-landing HEAD; read literally the sentence implies a rollback resolved the landed HEAD, which the document elsewhere rules out. The observable fact is that the reversed index/worktree persisted while HEAD carried the landing, not that the rollback read that HEAD.

follow-on: the gate log's first line reads 'revision: 7020130f0...' (the pre-fix commit) while its content ('production rollback:' and 'reckon rollback report:') is emitted only by the a5b62bac3 script, so the log does not name the revision of the code it ran, and a reader cannot reconcile the log's stated revision with its content. The command re-run at the reviewed head reproduces EXIT=0, so the substance is sound and only the stamped revision is off by one commit.
